newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM Cargo plans launch of three new productS.
newsitem.headline: KLM Cargo plans launch of three new productS.

text.p: KLM Cargo, the airfreight wing of KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV is planning to introduce a range of new airfreight products aimed at industrial shippers.

In the April edition of the company's magazine Cargovision, KLM says its newly created line haul unit (known in-house as its Rederij division) is currently finalising the definition of three new products.

KLM spokesman Peter Wellhuner said: "The first of the three is what we are calling an airside-to-airside product, which will be flight specific. This will cover airfreight which must be delivered to us ready for carriage. We will transport it to its destination airport where it must be picked by the addressee."

The second planned product he described as airport to airport service. "In this case, some freight handling will be involved - KLM would deliver the freight to an airport address - but shippers must have an airport address," said Wellhuner.
The third new product is also an airport to airport freight delivery service, but would be appropriate for less urgent consignments.
"Such freight would not be despatched on a flight specific basis. It affords us greater liberty, but would agree to move the freight in less than two days."
He said the planned new products are aimed at enhancing the airline's service to industrial shippers. Forwarders could also use the service, on behalf of big corporate accounts, he said.
The new products are the first planned by the new unit which was established April 1 and is responsible for KLM Cargo's route planning and sales.
Wellhuner could not specifically say when the products will be formally introduced to the market. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+April-5017
